items.title: Design: namespaces with pack-defined kinds (generalise beyond "component")
items.description: ## Status Restarted: supersedes #112 and its sub-issues (#128-#132), which were closed so work could begin again from a clean Wake state. Parent issue. The design is recorded in [PDR-008](https://github.com/atolis-hq/corum/blob/main/project/pdrs/PDR-008-namespaces-and-pack-defined-kinds.md) (accepted; its provisional items have been confirmed). This issue holds the requirements, acceptance criteria and guard rails, and is split into the sub-issues listed under **Work breakdown**. Dependencies #100 (via #120) and #121 (via #126) are done. It deliberately avoids implementation detail. ## Background Every node ID starts with a first segment that today is called the *component* (`orders.DomainModel.order`). In practice this segment is just a string. The grammar does not require it to be a software component, but the rest of the system assumes it is: - the on-disk folder is `components/` - the web UI groups the sidebar by `component`, has a `/components` route, and builds a component-level graph - the web API and MCP tools filter and report by `component` - docs and error messages describe the first segment as the component This blocks modelling things that are not components but live in their own right and span components: user journeys, event models, initiatives, and similar. A journey references components; it is not part of one. The goal is to let packs introduce such things without changing the engine, and to leave Corum architecture-first by default. ## Terminology (decided in PDR-008) - **Namespace**: the first ID segment. Owns the nodes beneath it. Generic, engine-level term (code, API, docs, grammar). - **Kind**: classification of a namespace, supplied by packs (`component`, `journey`, `event-model`, ...). Shown in the UI by its label. - **Component**: stays as the name of the default kind. It is no longer the generic term. Why "namespace": "scope" collides with existing graph UI thread/owner scoping, #56 and the extraction strategy; "domain", "context" and "cluster" already have meanings in Corum; "namespace" has no code collisions and describes exactly what the segment is. "Space" is the fallback if "namespace" proves too technical. The UI mostly shows kind labels, so the generic term appears rarely. ## Requirements 1. A namespace exists as soon as any node uses its prefix. No declaration is needed to get the default kind. 2. Every namespace has exactly one kind. An undeclared namespace has the default kind `component`. 3. Kinds are defined by packs,

items.title: devloop: ricevuta della PR con controllo di coerenza e invalidazione (#133, parte 3)
items.description: > [!NOTE] > **Agent:** Claude Code (CLI v2.1.322) > **Model:** Claude Opus 5.5 > **Reasoning Level:** High Parte 3 di 3 della richiesta dell'operatore del 2026-11-15. **Dipende da #133** (raccolta delle evidenze) e **da #134** (mappa dei criteri): entrambe devono essere su `main`. ## Obiettivo Al passaggio a `agent:ready-to-merge`, l'operatore che fa il merge vede in un colpo d'occhio: - cosa è stato chiesto; - chi ha fatto cosa, con quale modello e a quale costo; - cosa è stato verificato e su quale commit; - come si sono chiusi i finding; - come sono coperti i criteri. ## Requisiti - **Ricevuta.** La scrive il dispatcher, legata all'head approvato. Ha due forme: - un marker `receipt` con la sua identità, verificato in lettura come gli altri marker del dispatcher; - un commento leggibile nella PR, con l'intestazione AGENTS.md. - **Contenuto.** Viene **solo** dai record del dispatcher (#133) e dai marker, mai da testo scritto dagli agent: - lo snapshot della richiesta; - i turni con modello, durata, token e costo (`null` = "non riportato"); - gli eventi della CI e di sync; - le verifiche locali e della CI sull'head approvato; - i round, i verdetti per reviewer e i finding (`round/reviewer/ID`) con chi li ha chiusi; - la ricevuta di policy e il livello; - la mappa finale dei criteri (#134). - **Totali:** - numero di round e di turni; - durata sommata dei turni; - token e costo noti; - numero di turni con costo non riportato. La durata delle verifiche è separata. - **Coerenza:** - una **contraddizione** fra ricevuta e marker blocca la promozione (`agent:needs-human` con un commento); - i **dati storici assenti**, nelle PR avviate prima di #133, **non bloccano**: la ricevuta li dichiara mancanti. - **Invalidazione.** Se l'approvazione viene revocata, per esempio per un nuovo head o una ricevuta di policy diversa, il commento viene marcato come superato. La nuova promozione scrive una nuova ricevuta. ## Criteri di accettazione - [ ] Al passaggio a `agent:ready-to-merge` vengono pubblicati il marker e il commento leggibile, con tutte le sezioni. C'è un test con il fake di GitHub. - [ ] I valori non riportati compaiono come `null` o "non riportato", mai come 0. C'è un test. - [ ] Una contraddizione con i marker blocca la promozione. Dati storici assenti non la bloccano e vengono dichiarati. Ci sono test. - [ ] Una revoca seguita da una nuova promozione invalida la ricevuta precedente e ne scrive una nuova. C'è un test. - [ ] `docs/devloop.md` è aggiornato.

items.title: Abort signals on objects, stream, text and bytes
items.description: > *This was generated by AI during triage.* ## Problem `create`, `update` and `checkFixity` take an `AbortSignal`. The read calls don't, so a server can't stop reading a stored file when its client disconnects, and a long listing can't be cancelled. ## Proposed change All additive: `objects()`, `text()` and `bytes()` take no options today, and `file.stream` already takes `StreamOptions`. Decided in triage: - `root.purge` and `UnfinishedWrite.recover` get no signal. Once either starts deleting, it must finish, so a signal could only cancel the short checks before that. It can be added later without a breaking change. - `draft.import` needs no signal of its own: the update's signal already stops it between files. Progress on `import` moved to its own issue, #454. ## Original request **Title:** Abort signals on remove, objects, stream, text, bytes and recover; progress on import ## Problem `create`, `update` and `checkFixity` take an `AbortSignal`. Other long-running calls don't, and `import` reports no progress. ## Proposed change All additive: `remove(id)` and `objects()` take no options today, and `file.stream` gets an options type in #367. `text()`, `bytes()` and `UnfinishedWrite.recover()` can take `(options?)` the same way. --- From the pre-1.0 review of November 2026. File and line references were correct at `6dc9df2`; check them before relying on them.

items.title: Pin replaces Flag: product Pins in the reader, message lists and sidebar
items.description: ## What to build Owner decision of 13 November 2026: the interface says **Pin, never Flag**. There is no Flagged mailbox, the reader toolbar shows the pin symbol, and a pinned Thread's row carries the pin marker in `status/warning`. - Mac Inbox ([Light](https://www.figma.com/design/d1mHEaUNmnF7YUw6QwIs0T?node-id=13-36) · [Dark](https://www.figma.com/design/d1mHEaUNmnF7YUw6QwIs0T?node-id=17-2740)): `pin` in the reader toolbar, `pin.fill` on message rows, **Pins** in Favorites after Snoozed. - Mac Sidebar — Edit Favorites ([Light](https://www.figma.com/design/d1mHEaUNmnF7YUw6QwIs0T?node-id=150-42793) · [Dark](https://www.figma.com/design/d1mHEaUNmnF7YUw6QwIs0T?node-id=150-43353)): the Flagged row is gone and the row reads Pins. - iPad and iPhone menus read Pin with the pin symbol (for example iPad [127:35523](https://www.figma.com/design/d1mHEaUNmnF7YUw6QwIs0T?node-id=127-35523)); iPhone Mailboxes Edit lists Pins and no Flagged. A **Pin** is the product's own marker on a **Thread**, synchronized through **Private Sync** and independent of provider flags (`docs/domain/organization.md`, `docs/product/organization.md` › Pins). `docs/product/mailboxes.md` lists Pins among the permanent Unified Mailboxes. The maintained clients have no Pin yet. ## Today - What the clients call Flag is the provider's star: Gmail `STARRED` and IMAP `\Flagged` (`star` and `unstar` in `packages/mail-core/src/gmail-actions.ts` and `imap-actions.ts`). - Labels: `contextMenu.star` "Flag", `contextMenu.unstar` "Unflag", `gmailActions.label.star` "Star", `inbox.rowLabel_flagged*` "Flagged", `mailboxes.flagged` "Flagged". - Symbols: `flag` and `flag.fill` in `apps/macos/src/organize.tsx`, `flag` and `flag.slash` in `apps/mobile/src/organize.tsx`, and a `flag.fill` row marker in `apps/macos/src/inbox-rows.tsx` and `apps/mobile/src/inbox-rows.tsx`. - The sidebar's Favorites come from `unifiedRoles` in `packages/mail-core/src/mailbox-views.ts` (Sent, Archive, All Mail, Spam, Trash); there is no Pins view. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] Pin and Unpin act on the Thread, are stored as product state through Private Sync as `docs/product/organization.md` › Pins requires, work offline, and never change a provider flag. - [ ] The reader toolbar, the message and Thread context menus, the Command Palette and VoiceOver actions offer **Pin** and **Unpin** with `pin` and `pin.slash` on Mac, iPad and iPhone, for every provider. - [ ] A pinned Thread's row shows `pin.fill` in `status/warning`, and VoiceOver

items.title: Axis unit conversion: an affine display transform for tick labels
items.description: A plan, to be approved here before code (rule 7). ## Goal An axis can show its values in another unit without the host converting the data: the labels read `shown = scale * value + offset`. Examples: raw ADC counts shown as volts, kelvin shown as degrees Celsius, seconds shown as milliseconds. The data, the column pool and every data-unit setting stay as they are; only what the axis prints changes. This also covers calibration for #271: raw `i16` channels stay raw and the axis prints physical units. This is appearance under rule 1, as `LabelFormat::Percent` already shows value × 100: the renderer prints the given data in another unit and produces no new data values. ## Model - `AxisOptions` gets an additive field, for example `unit: Option ` with `AxisUnit { scale: f64, offset: f64 }`. - It is `None` by default and serialized only when set, so older documents read and re-serialize unchanged. - It is a new field on a public struct, so the CHANGELOG gets a migration note for Rust literals. - Validation (`ConfigError`): - `scale` must be finite and non-zero; `offset` must be finite. - A negative `scale` is allowed: the printed values then decrease along the axis. - Any axis built on `AxisOptions` takes it: the Cartesian axes, overlay axes, the colour bar axis, and the polar radial axis where it prints numbers. ## What changes and what does not **Unchanged, in data units:** - `min` and `max`; - the data and the pool; - annotation positions; - axis breaks; - pick results (series id and index). **Converted, in shown units:** - **Tick plan:** nice steps are chosen in shown units over `[scale*min+offset, scale*max+offset]`, so the labels read `0, 0.5, 1.0 V`, not converted counts. Each tick is placed at `value = (shown - offset) / scale`. - **`major_spacing`:** when it is set, it is read in shown units. - **Tick labels:** formatted from the shown value with the axis' `LabelFormat`. - **Readouts of that axis:** the hover and coordinate readouts the renderer formats for the axis. **Layout:** `auto_layout`, hit testing, selection and drag all use the same label emission, so they follow the converted labels with no separate path. ## Scales - A linear axis takes any valid `scale` and `offset`. - **Log axis:** only `offset = 0` and `scale > 0`, since an offset or a sign flip has no log meaning. Ticks stay at decades of the shown value. - **Rejected with an explicit error:** probability axes, `Timestamp` labels and categorical axes. ## Surfaces (rule 6) - **Rust:** a hel

items.title: A hub view over declared membership: hub members, stale hubs, orphans (spike first; generate needs a decision)
items.description: Item 9 of #1680 (native task-queue commands for agents). **Spike first, and one design decision for the maintainer.** **The problem.** A research KB grows hundreds of finding notes. Readers start from hub pages (a beat, a case, a contract, a facility), each listing the notes that belong to it. Keeping hubs true by hand fails three ways: - a new note is never listed on any hub (an orphan); - a hub lists notes that were superseded, or misses notes that joined; - each script that checks this defines "orphan" differently. A prototype outside the repository had three definitions before it settled on one. **Wanted:** a hub view over backlinks: show a hub's members, report stale hubs, report orphans. The prototype also *generates* the listing into the hub page; that part needs the decision below. ## Groom 2026-11-17 *Checked on `dev` at `ebc161f2`.* **User's model:** "A note says which hubs it belongs to. Show me each hub's members, the hubs whose page is out of date, and the notes on no hub." **Implementation model:** membership is declared on the member's own side, as a field whose values are hub ids. Pyrite already indexes such a field as a reference when the schema declares it `object-ref`. The view is a query over that index: derived, written nowhere. ### 1. Contracts that apply - `kb/design.md` principle 4: what can be computed from the files is derived and shown as derived. Members, staleness and orphans qualify. **A listing generated into the hub's file is a derived value written into a file.** See Decision. - Principle 1: the files are the KB, and any tool can read them. That is the case *for* generating: a reader on GitHub or a static site sees only the files. - Principle 7: which types are hubs and which field declares membership is the operator's configuration (kb.yaml). - `kb/maps/links-blocks-collections-and-formats.md` and `kb/maps/types-and-schema.md`: links, `object-ref` fields and the `entry_ref` index. ### 2. What the code does today - An `object-ref` field declared in kb.yaml is indexed into the `entry_ref` table (`pyrite/storage/index.py`, the "Extract object-ref fields" step). Reverse references are queryable (`pyrite/storage/queries.py`, "entries that reference this entry via object-ref fields"; `pyrite/services/graph_service.py`). - `pyrite backlinks ` lists entries that link to an id, through any link. The prototype deliberately does **not** count plain inbound links: a link from a task does not put a note on a hub. - `pyrite links orphan

items.title: Monotonic-x line chart: its own source and rules, M4 decimation per pixel column (after 0.19)
items.description: Not for 0.19. A plan to measure and refine before any code. ## Goal A line chart for fast, large, evenly spaced data (x = `start + i * interval`, strictly increasing), drawn losslessly at display resolution: per pixel column the renderer reduces the samples to **M4** (first, min, max, last), and the GPU draws only about `4 × plot width` vertices. The result must be pixel-identical to drawing every segment. Only lines; scatter is out of scope, because min/max per column drops the points between them. ## Source A new source trait for this chart only (not `ColumnSource`), for example `MonotonicSource`: - `values() -> &[f64]` (or chunks), `len()` - `start() -> f64`, `interval() -> f64` (> 0) - `generation() -> u64`: moves on any change that is not an append. An append only grows `len()`. The renderer reads the host's data through the trait when it reduces; the data is not uploaded to the column pool. ## Reduction and cache - Pixel column of sample `i`: `floor((start + i*interval - x_min) / x_per_pixel)`. Plain arithmetic, no search. - Per series the renderer CPU keeps the M4 envelope **in data units** (4 values per pixel column) and the scalars it was computed with: `start`, `interval`, `x_min`, `x_per_pixel`, plot width, valid `len`, `generation`. - **Tail only:** when `start`, `interval`, `generation`, x range and plot width are unchanged and `len` grew. It recomputes from the last (partial) pixel column to the new end. - **Full:** when any of those changed. - **Free:** a y-range change. The envelope is in data units, so only the projection changes; it happens in the shader. - Reduction on the CPU with chunked loops written to auto-vectorize. A SIMD crate is added only if a measurement shows the loops fall short. - The staleness check uses the **generation** pattern from "Identity and staleness checks" in `crates/renderer/ARCHITECTURE.md`; no new pattern. ## Rules for this source (a separate rule set, not exceptions) To be added to `CLAUDE.md` as its own section with the feature. It applies only to `MonotonicSource` line series; rules 1, 2, 5 and 8 keep governing every other series. - **M1. Input.** Data enters only through `MonotonicSource`: values, start, interval and generation. No other container. - **M2. Reduction is appearance.** The renderer may reduce to M4 per pixel column. The drawn image must equal drawing every segment; a test compares the two at 1x and 2x, across magnitudes, NaN gaps and partial columns. - **M3. Cache bound.** The CPU cache hold

items.title: auto_layout: fit bands both ways, pad the title, measure overhangs and group headers
items.description: ## Why Every example was switched to `Chart::fit_layout()` (`layout::auto_layout`) and each of about 100 renders was compared with its hand-laid-out version. Auto layout is good at growing a band that is too small (clipped category labels, axis titles over tick labels, colour-bar titles, subplots, overlay axes, 3D box labels, break pieces). But four structural gaps make it unfit as the default layout: 1. **Bands never shrink** (`fit_band`: `before.max(grown)`). Without hand margins every chart keeps the defaults (left 110, bottom 80, overlay 110). Hidden-frame and annotation-only charts (Feynman, math gallery) end up lopsided. Charts without an axis title keep ~100 px of empty band. Document charts (`from_categorical`/`from_boxplot`/`from_radar`) do not change at all. 2. **No room around the chart title** (`fit_chart_title_margin` acts only when the title is taller than its band, then adds 4 px). Nearly every render has its title 0–3 px from the top edge; a title-less chart keeps a 32 px band. 3. **No outer padding**: a grown band ends `LABEL_GAP` past its labels, so labels sit ~5 px from the chart edge (lollipop). 4. **Overhang and group headers are not measured**: the top/bottom y tick labels poke half their height past the plot into the title band; `CategoryGroupLabel` rows are not probed, so an x title is placed on the header row (Grotrian "J"). Ternary charts also lose: the triangle reserves its own label room inside the data area, and the default bottom band is stacked on top (item 1 fixes it). ## Plan (only `crates/model/src/layout/geometry.rs` and its tests/docs) - **A. Exact bands.** In `auto_layout`, every band (four axes, overlays, colour bar) is set to what it needs, smaller or larger: labels' reach + `LABEL_GAP` + title + an outer edge padding; a side with nothing to hold gets the edge padding only. The guard that refuses a band leaving no data area stays. The "never shrunk" contract of `auto_layout` is dropped (it is unreleased, 0.19). `fit_chart_title_margin`, which `with_title`/`set_title` use, is unchanged. - **B. Title band.** `auto_layout` sets `chart_title.top_margin` to the title's measured height plus padding above and below proportional to its font size; a hidden or empty title gets 0 (the top band then holds the top padding). - **C. Outer edge padding**: one constant at the outer edge of every fitted band. - **D. items.title: Roadmap 2d: fusion sites as priced candidates of the one cost model
items.description: **Product goal.** The user names the model, the quantization, the number of concurrent streams and the context. We choose everything else, optimally for their card, from the card's published facts and the kernels' counted facts. There is no measurement on the user's card, and ideally none on every card of every series. Lab measurements verify the theory; a mismatch fixes the model, never a fitted constant. ## Why - **Twelve fusion sites live in twelve files with local rules**, and three of them rest on one card. - **The real "MMQ fused gate/up" is not one launch.** It is a plane write plus a second epilogue launch: the first chain worth pricing. - **KV write and residual+norm are already fused** for dense and Gemma. - **The launch cost is already measured per generation** (`choice_constants.h:172`, `round_cost.h:169`). #603 says no constant is fitted, which is wrong. - **#603's tie of 1e-9** should be #600's resolution. ## Decision (F2′) - Every fusion site is registered with its alternatives, its byte promise (Equal/OwnOrder) and its invariant-profile pin. - Every fused kernel becomes a route of the generic selector, so the same tile, wave, split-K and warp-fill terms price it. - One `launch_node_seconds(generation, pdl)` is shared by the choice, the speculation code and #603. - A graph planner (F3) is not worth it. Fixed recipes (F4) only as the fallback for an unknown generation. ## Steps A, B and C are host-only and can run in parallel. D follows them, E–H can then run in parallel, and I–K are ordered by predicted value. - [x] **A.** Registry data plus a host test. (#638) - [x] **B.** One launch-node constant. Done in #651. - [x] **C.** #603's tie rule becomes #600's resolution, and its comment on the launch constant is corrected. Required before #603 merges. #603 - [ ] **D.** The Q8 pair as a priced route, with a replica test against #565. **GPU 1 h.** - [ ] **E.** Wire linear_pair. **GPU 2 h.** - [x] **F.** Wire the SwiGLU pair against separate launches. **GPU 2 h.** Closed with evidence (18.11): a same-format gate/up is packed and runs linear_swiglu, the fused alternative; the MMQ gated pair runs only for a two-format gate/up, which no shipped artifact has. Within its band it dominates term by term. Two A/Bs on the 5070 Ti (Qwen3.5-9B, Qwen3-8B) are flat. - [x] **G.** rmsnorm_rope's bound from a wave rule, instead of the 256 measured on the 5090 only. **GPU 1 h.** Done in #661 (law in place, uncalibrated: every board keeps 256; open points #720). -

items.title: Sidebar search: magnifier on the Temporary Rooms header and filter temporary rooms

items.title: Add Swahili (sw) widget translation
items.description: The widget ships five strings in 34 languages. Swahili isn't one of them yet. **What to do** Add a `sw` entry to the `I18N` table in `client/fcaptcha.js`. Each entry is five strings, in this order: 1. `label`: the resting checkbox label ("I'm not a robot") 2. `verifying`: shown while checking ("Verifying…") 3. `verified`: shown on success ("Verified") 4. `failed`: shown on failure ("Verification failed") 5. `retry`: shown before the widget resets ("Verification failed. Please try again.") Copy the shape of an existing entry such as `de`. Please only take this on if you're a fluent speaker; machine translations of short UI strings tend to read oddly. **Done when** - `FCaptcha.render(el, { siteKey, lang: 'sw' })` shows your strings - `cd test/browser && CI=1 npx playwright test i18n` passes - The language count in the README's feature list is updated

items.title: Ask HN: UK Equivalent for Power Switch Tail/IoT Power Relay?
items.description: Basically I just want a 230 volt relay that I can turn on/off with a Raspberry Pi/Ardunio, but I don't feel confident enough to tinker with mains electricity myself. I saw the Powerswitch tail 2 (https://www.adafruit.com/product/268) a while ago, which has been discontinued but replaced with the IoT Power Relay (https://www.adafruit.com/product/2935). Both look great, the problem is that they're only made for US plugs at American voltage and I want something I can use with a UK plug. Anyone know of anything for this? I have a few Wi-Fi smart plugs but I'd like something simple that I can hardwire and control myself without any wireless connectivity. Just a pre-made relay cable. This feels like something I should be able to easily find online but I guess I'm just bad at googling?

items.title: Ask HN: Anyone else blurting?
items.description: Like most, I was stoked on LLMs when they became available. Particularly on the earlier free tiers where the slightly questionable answers were offset by generous tokens. Now, I'm finding that having to use this tech is becoming much less fun. The constant corrections, the constant prompting for greater brevity, the grating certainty and sycophancy. Others probably are forgiving considering the net benefit. But for me it honestly now feels like a chore, which is reflected in how my frustration is now appearing in how I communicate to it now. Instead of articulating and making my prompts precise, I'm just straight-out blurting. Typos, missed words, poor semantic structure - I guess I maybe at some point reasoned that "it will get the picture, so why waste effort being articulate?" Or maybe I'm just anticipating that it is going to get it 15 percent wrong, so why even try and be articulate. Just blurt and steer. Blurt and steer. Is anyone else finding this? I actually sometimes worry about it. I feel it's not just the fact that I'm offloading my cognition to it that is making me dumber, it is the way I'm communicating with it. They say the act of writing is tied to the act of thinking, and my prompts are basicslly the typographic equivalent of grunting right now.

These areas were key factors in our decision not to move forward. Which I find very funny. What was yours?

items.title: Ask HN: Do you still enjoy coding in C++?
items.description: In the recent years C++ received a lot of backlash due to its complexity and (perceived) feature creep. However, since C++11 I really enjoyed writing C++ with its strict type system (including const), range-based for loops, smart pointers, and how much you can do with templates. On the other hand, I know that it can be very tricky to write, for instance, a correct iterator, to get handling of rvalue references right, or to read error messages that involve templates. So, do you enjoy or dislike writing C++ source code and why?
